solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stay in Dallas involved festival

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of these three words are mixed together

explanation.surface: Someone advises staying put in Dallas for a big celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges STAYINDALLAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of November is a Christian feast day honouring every saint, so it is a church festival.

clue.text: Threescore years and ten — if energy's left first, sleep's taken over

indicators.note: first says the left letter goes at the front, before the other pieces

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

indicators.note: taken over means turned upside down, which reverses a down entry

parts.note: naps are short sleeps, and the 's adds the plural letter

explanation.surface: A wordy reflection on a person's allotted seventy years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken over' reverses NAPS. 'Threescore years and ten' is the Bible's seventy-year span (Psalm 90).
explanation.definitionFit: Seventy years is the traditional biblical allotment of a human life, its whole duration.

clue.text: Agile mole grabs gopher's tail

indicators.note: grabs means the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: tail means the last letter of gopher is taken

explanation.surface: A nimble little mole seizes a gopher by the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' looks like an animal beside the gopher, but it is a spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimble and lively, especially of an older person, so it is a synonym of agile.

clue.text: Ten crimes solved — number getting framed increases

indicators.note: getting framed means a letter is put inside, surrounded like a picture
solved means worked out, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten crimes are cleared up, and one suspect is framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solved' rearranges TENCRIMES; 'getting framed' places N inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Increments are additions or steps upward, which is what increases are as nouns.

clue.text: Mass of seaweed

definitions.meaning: a confused, knotted heap of something
a name for kelp-type brown seaweed with long fronds

explanation.surface: A clump of weed from the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a knotted heap and also names a type of kelp.

clue.text: Hippie in Germany put work into retreat

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

indicators.note: into says the work is placed inside the retreat

parts.note: a rout is a disorderly retreat after defeat
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A German hippie gets a job in a hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' suggests a hideaway, but here it is a rout, a headlong flight.
explanation.definitionFit: A hippie rejects conventional society, which is the sense of someone who has turned their back on the system.

clue.text: In exuberant style Rome may well start to hang bunting

indicators.note: exuberant style means wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order
start to means the first letter of hang is taken

explanation.surface: Rome may hang festive flags with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives H, added to ROMEMAYWELL; 'In exuberant style' rearranges them all. 'bunting' looks like flags but is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Buntings are a family of finch-like birds, and this yellow-headed one is among them.

clue.text: Up-and-down experience in the present and past

parts.note: to see something is to experience it, and see is the present tense
saw is the past tense of the same verb

explanation.surface: Life's ups and downs, felt now and before.
explanation.walkthrough: One verb, see, is given in two tenses.
explanation.definitionFit: A plank on a pivot swings riders alternately high and low, a back-and-forth motion.

clue.text: Slave switched direction to discover identity

indicators.note: the direction letter for right is swapped for the one for left

parts.note: a serf was a bonded labourer, effectively a slave

explanation.surface: A slave who changes course finds out who they really are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switched direction' swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: One's self is one's own person, so self is a synonym of personal identity.

clue.text: Shock associated with northern turn's music

parts.note: to rock someone is to shock them
a roll is a turn over, as of a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: A northern music-hall act's music causes a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface a 'turn' is a stage act; here it is a roll.
explanation.definitionFit: The popular genre of the 1950s, with its heavy beat, is a style of music.

clue.text: Eyeing up the girls may cause twitching

definitions.text: Eyeing up the girls may cause twitching

parts.words: Eyeing up the girls may cause twitching
parts.note: birds is slang for young women, and twitching is the enthusiast's term for spotting rare species

explanation.surface: Ogling women might give you a nervous tic.
explanation.walkthrough: Bird is British slang for a young woman; a twitcher chases rare bird sightings.
explanation.definitionFit: Watching feathered birds is the hobby, and slang birds are young women, so both readings fit.

clue.text: To maintain central core of gas mains is tricky

indicators.note: the answer sits deep inside these words, held in their middle rather than at either end

explanation.surface: Someone claims that servicing the heart of the gas network is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'mains is tricky'.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain a claim is to keep asserting it firmly, which is what insisting means.

clue.text: We old lot could be quids in!

indicators.note: could be means these letters might become something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: Elderly people imagine themselves as winners of a windfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges WEOLDLOT. 'Quids in' is British slang for being in profit; a quid is a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quids in means having money to spare, so it describes the comfortably wealthy.

clue.text: Groups in braces put on singles?

definitions.text: Groups in braces put on singles?

parts.words: Groups in braces put on singles?
parts.note: a brace is a pair, and a pair added to a single makes a group of three

explanation.surface: Bands that wear braces playing on singles records.
explanation.walkthrough: A brace is two; two plus a single is three.
explanation.definitionFit: Groups of three people or things are trios, built as two plus one.

clue.text: In a sorry state, depressed athlete missing a little time for training

parts.note: feeling down means feeling depressed

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the remaining letters are put into a new order
missing means the athlete is without one letter

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time; little means just the one letter

explanation.surface: An athlete is miserable after a short spell away from training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops T from ATHLETE, leaving ATHLEE, which 'for training' rearranges to ATHEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby and run-down, like a shoe worn at the back, so the idiom means in poor condition.

clue.text: Initially iodine treatment can heal skin infection

indicators.note: initially means the opening letters of the next four words are taken

explanation.surface: Iodine applied early can cure a skin complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' takes the first letters of 'iodine treatment can heal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word also names a contagious skin complaint such as scabies, not just an irritation.

clue.text: Huge mistake to block right to get a raise in charge

indicators.note: block means the mistake sits inside, stopping up the other word
in a down clue a raise lifts the word so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: fit means right or proper
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A big blunder blocks someone's rightful pay rise in their post.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'get a raise' turns the word upward, giving TIF; 'raise' in the surface is a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant causing terror and so means enormous or intense.

clue.text: Spiritual stronghold

definitions.meaning: an old poetic word for airy or ethereal, not of the body
a variant spelling of eyrie, an eagle's high nest and so a lofty stronghold

explanation.surface: A sanctuary of the spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves both as an adjective for ethereal things and a variant of eyrie, a lofty fortress.

clue.text: Walker who goes on and on

definitions.meaning: someone who hikes in the countryside for pleasure
a person who talks at length without getting to the point

explanation.surface: A hiker who never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on and on' reads as walking but means talking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hikers and long-winded talkers both wander at length.

clue.text: Instrument found in boiler house

parts.note: a kettle is a vessel for boiling water
drum is slang for a house or home

explanation.surface: A musical instrument turns up in the boiler room of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: Drum for a house is old British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A timpano, the orchestra's large tuned drum, is a percussion instrument.

clue.text: Covered in blood, rower shouted noisily

indicators.note: covered in means the rower is placed inside the colour

parts.note: red is the colour of blood
an oar can mean an oarsman, someone who rows

explanation.surface: A bloodied rower yelled loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rower' is a person in the surface but here is OAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Roared means bellowed, gave a loud deep shout.

clue.text: Street above York put up flashing light

indicators.note: above means in a down entry the street comes first, on top
put up means the word is lifted to read bottom to top in a down entry

parts.note: Ebor is short for Eboracum, the Latin name for York

explanation.surface: A York street installs a flashing light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses EBOR to ROBE.
explanation.definitionFit: A strobe is a lamp emitting rapid regular pulses, so it is a light that flashes.

clue.text: Rendered unconscious from combination of oxygen, steam and carbon monoxide

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula of carbon monoxide

indicators.note: a combination mixes things up, so these letters are rearranged together

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A chemistry-lab mishap: a toxic mix of gases knocks someone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'combination of' makes MATOSE. The clue lists carbon monoxide last, but its formula opens the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in a coma is deeply unconscious, so the adjective fits being knocked out.

clue.text: Film of oily matter

definitions.meaning: the 1978 musical movie starring John Travolta and Olivia Newton-John
fat or lubricant, a thick slippery substance

explanation.surface: A thin coating of something oily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' reads as a thin layer but is a movie title.
explanation.definitionFit: The movie title and the word for fat or lubricant share one spelling.

clue.text: One's against being kept in quarantine

indicators.note: the letters are held within the next word

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to being confined in quarantine.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'quarantine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone opposed is an opponent; the word is used as a noun for such a person.

clue.text: Dependency on self? I am confused

indicators.note: confused means jumbled, so these letters are mixed up together

explanation.surface: Someone muddled admits being dependent on themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges ONSELFIAM. 'Dependency' looks abstract but is a territory.
explanation.definitionFit: The island in the Irish Sea is a Crown Dependency, self-governing but under the British Crown.

clue.text: Paid for food

definitions.meaning: read as ..., given a fee, that is paid
fodder or a meal, especially for animals or babies

explanation.surface: Someone has paid for something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paid' is a pun: fee'd, having received a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as fee'd it means remunerated; as a noun it means a meal or fodder.

clue.text: One's used in knitting leg-bands — 16 will go round top of thigh

indicators.note: the two pieces sit on either side, surrounding a single letter

parts.note: garters are elastic bands worn round the leg
16 refers to the answer to 16 Across, a skin complaint

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of thigh is taken

explanation.surface: Knitted leg-bands make the top of the thigh itch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will go round' has both pieces, not one, enclose the letter; '16' points to the answer at 16 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain knitting on every row produces a ridged fabric; this is the name of that basic stitch.
